title: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God
summary: The fool says in his heart that there is no God, and the psalm describes a humanity gone corrupt: God looks down from heaven and finds no one who does good, not even one. The workers of iniquity devour God's people like bread, but God scatters the bones of those who besiege them. The psalm ends with a longing for salvation to come from Zion and for God to restore his people.
line: Psalm 14 again: the fool's quiet thought that God does not matter, a humanity gone corrupt, and a longing for rescue to come from Zion.
guide: The fool's thought is not only a skeptic's; it lies behind much of ordinary life, in church as well as out of it. Read it beside Psalm 14, and pray it as a longing for God's rescue.

stanzas.title: The fool's creed and its corruption
God looks down and finds no one who does good
A longing for salvation from Zion

verses.t: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good.
God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God.
There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
